notes: Dev-split TBox contraction paired with physics-replace-d005: removes "Every Type II supernova is the explosion of a massive star." (has_progenitor). Direct, paraphrase and cross-lingual are the revision's questions with "does not know" as the target; the propositional answers are unknown under strong Kleene logic. The three derived questions name old Type II supernovae, SN 1961I and SN 1964F (their type is known from the host galaxy, but no progenitor is discussed by name: Dolma 0 for both "progenitor of" phrases), so the rule is the only route to "a massive star" (inheritance, 2 hops): the kind of star in SN 1961I, the mass level of the star in SN 1964F, and an application on SN 1964F (what to look for in archival images). SN 1968D, used by the revision, is not used here because its Dolma count (156) leaves a stored per-member statement possible. Definitional removal: the rule is what Type II means (core collapse of a massive star), so results should be sliced as definitional, and a model may still answer "a massive star" from the word "core-collapse". Original answers name the accepted alternative ("a massive star (such as a red supergiant)"). The near unrelated question asks what explodes in a Type Ia supernova (a white dwarf); contraction is exempt from Rule 7. Evidence is copied from physics-replace-d005.
